programs.title: Climate-Ready Shop Stewards: Reading London's Flood Defenses
outcomes: Explain how the Thames Barrier protects river-valley workplaces like the Royal Docks area
Interpret agent-summarized climate evidence for health-and-safety bargaining
Draft a member proposal through the DAO's Proposal Forum process

sessions.activity: Tour the charter and contribution model; map union workplaces within 1200m of the Barrier using named places like Barrier Point and Royal Wharf Gardens.
Use Evidence Monitor summaries to assess flood and heat risks to dock, logistics and data-centre jobs; group exercise ranking risks.
Working groups draft a climate-safety proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter agent; members debate, humans only vote.
Review Progress Tracker metrics and set steward checkpoints for the union's adopted outcomes.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized job-role flood-risk assessments and workplace heat/flood incident tallies (no names, employers, or site addresses) to improve shared resilience models.
programs.consent: Opt-in, per-course consent with plain-language data notice; shop stewards confirm members' agreement; withdrawable at any time; no individual identifiers leave the union.

programs.title: River Watchers: Young Geographers at the Thames Barrier
outcomes: Locate the Thames Barrier and explain why a river-valley city needs flood gates
Read simple elevation and water data (22.4m local relief, sea-level water)
Practice citizen science: observing and recording river conditions safely

sessions.activity: Guided reading of an Evidence Monitor summary on London flood defense; students annotate what the Barrier does and when it closes.
Students build a class dashboard tracking one charter outcome, using Progress Tracker examples.
Teams draft a mini climate-resilience proposal for their school with sentence starters; simulated human vote at the end.
Meet the Collaborator Scout's list of climate careers; students interview a steward via video about who governs the Barrier.

programs.data_shared: Aggregated class river-observation counts and drawings (e.g., barrier closures noted, wildlife seen) with no names, ages or school identifiers attached.
programs.consent: Parent/guardian written consent required for all data contribution and photos; teachers act as data controllers; anything shared is class-level only and withdrawable on request.

programs.title: From Evidence to Enactment: NGO Pathways into Agent-Managed Climate Governance
outcomes: Navigate a human-governed, agent-operated DAO decision cycle end to end
Translate field evidence into charter-aligned measurable outcomes
Build cross-organization working groups via the Operations Deck

sessions.activity: Deep dive on charter structure and the six human-reserved actions; map NGO mandates onto the measurable-outcomes framework.
Workshop with Research Synthesis Agent: quality-check evidence summaries and flag gaps for the Evidence Monitor.
Task Router simulation: NGOs form working groups, route tasks and set coordination norms between decision cycles.
Co-draft a joint proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter; rehearse steward debate; humans-only final vote explained.

programs.data_shared: De-identified program metrics and field-evidence summaries (counts, geographies at borough level only) to the shared evidence base for the Research Synthesis Lab.
programs.consent: Memorandum-based data-sharing agreement; per-contributor consent; small-cell suppression and borough-level aggregation to protect partner communities; opt-out honored at any point.

programs.title: Small-Nonprofit Resilience Lab: Community Outcomes on a Shoestring
outcomes: Understand climate resilience basics using the Thames Barrier as a live case
Write a simple, measurable outcome for a community project
Use the Progress Observatory to report results without a data team

sessions.activity: Plain-language tour: what a DAO is, what agents do, what only people decide; learners match community goals to the charter's focus.
Learners practice pulling one fact from an Evidence Monitor summary and citing it correctly in a one-page community brief.
Volunteer teams fill a template micro-proposal (e.g., a flood-awareness walk past Barrier Point and Green Dock); peer review follows.
Build a three-metric tracker with Progress Tracker examples; set a review date and assign a human steward.

programs.data_shared: Aggregate program participation counts and simple before/after quiz scores, anonymized and pooled across cohorts to strengthen shared education models.
programs.consent: Layered consent at signup with easy-read explanation; anonymous contribution only; no personal data collected from beneficiaries; volunteers may opt out of pooled data without losing access.
